text.zh-CN: 自杀意念是关于结束自己生命的想法，可从觉得“不如不在了”到反复思考或形成计划。它是需要认真回应的症状，可能伴随多种疾病或生活危机；有想法并不等于已经发生自杀行为。
text.en: Suicidal ideation means thoughts about ending one's life, ranging from wishing not to be alive to repeated thoughts or plans. It is a symptom requiring a serious response and can accompany several illnesses or life crises; thoughts are distinct from an act.

text.zh-CN: 这些想法可挤占注意力、影响睡眠、关系和学习工作。支持与治疗能帮助人度过危机；评估既要看此刻是否可能行动，也要查清持续痛苦的来源。
text.en: These thoughts can occupy attention and disrupt sleep, relationships, study and work. Support and treatment can help a person through a crisis; assessment addresses both immediate potential for action and the sources of distress.

text.zh-CN: 抑郁、双相障碍、酒精或其他物质使用问题、慢性疼痛，以及丧失、冲突、暴力或经济压力，都可能参与其中。不能只凭自杀想法就认定是抑郁症，也不能因没有精神科诊断就忽略危机。
text.en: Depression, bipolar disorder, alcohol or other substance problems, chronic pain, loss, conflict, violence and financial stress can contribute. Suicidal thoughts alone do not establish depression, and lack of a psychiatric diagnosis does not remove the need for help.

text.zh-CN: 过去有自杀行为、家族史或长期创伤经历，需要告诉评估者。它们是背景线索，不是注定会发生的结果；突然增强的冲动、孤立、失眠或物质使用是更需要及时处理的变化。
text.en: Tell the assessor about previous suicidal behaviour, family history or lasting trauma. These are background clues rather than destiny; increasing impulses, isolation, sleep disruption or substance use are changes needing timely attention.

text.zh-CN: 已经伤害自己、准备很快行动，或感觉控制不住冲动、无法保证当下安全时，立即联系当地急救或到急诊；请可信的人陪着，不独处。帮助者应在自身安全的前提下陪伴并呼救。
text.en: After self-injury, when preparing to act soon, or when impulses feel uncontrollable and immediate safety cannot be maintained, contact local emergency services or go to an emergency department. Ask a trusted person to stay; helpers should remain and call for help when safe to do so.

text.zh-CN: 正在出现自杀想法，应立即联系危机服务或医疗人员，由专业人员判断是否需要紧急评估；如果有行动意图或无法保持安全，按急救处理。不要用“还没有具体计划”作为继续独自等待的理由。
text.en: For current suicidal thoughts, contact crisis or clinical services now to determine whether an urgent assessment is needed. Intent to act or inability to remain safe requires emergency care; absence of a detailed plan is not a reason to wait alone.

text.en: In mainland China,12356 provides psychological support; in the US, call or text988; in the UK, NHS111 can direct urgent mental-health care and Samaritans is116123. Immediate life-threatening danger requires local emergency services rather than waiting for a helpline.

text.zh-CN: 问卷可以开启谈话，却不能准确预言某个人是否会行动。英国NICE在自伤后评估中明确反对仅凭分数或“低中高风险”标签决定治疗和出院；要结合本人经历、当前变化及实际安全条件。
text.en: A questionnaire can start a conversation but cannot accurately predict an individual act. UK NICE guidance after self-harm advises against using scores or low/medium/high labels alone to decide treatment or discharge; the person's account, current changes and practical safety matter.

text.zh-CN: 临床团队根据安全条件安排急诊、住院或门诊；同时处理已发生的身体损伤、物质使用、疼痛和精神疾病。治疗场所取决于当下需要，不是所有想法都自动需要住院，也不是一句否认就足以出院。
text.en: The team arranges emergency, inpatient or outpatient care according to safety and treats injury, substance problems, pain and mental illness. Thoughts do not automatically mean admission, and a single denial does not establish readiness for discharge.

text.zh-CN: 认知行为治疗帮助识别困住自己的思维并练习其他应对方式；辩证行为治疗侧重情绪和应对技能，对部分反复自伤的青少年及成人特定人群有证据。方法要结合年龄、相关疾病和既往行为选择。
text.en: Cognitive behavioural therapy builds alternative responses to difficult thought patterns. Dialectical behaviour therapy teaches emotional and coping skills, with evidence in some adolescents with repeated self-harm and selected adult populations. Choice depends on age, associated illness and behaviour history.

text.zh-CN: 共同写一份可随手查看的安全计划：个人警示信号、可行的缓解步骤、可以去的安全地方、可联系的人和紧急服务，以及如何减少危险物品的可及性。具体计划比只要求“保证不做傻事”更有用。
text.en: Create an accessible safety plan together: personal warning signs, feasible coping steps, safe places, people and emergency services to contact, and reduced access to dangerous items. Use a practical plan rather than a promise not to act.

text.zh-CN: SSRI等抗抑郁药用于合适的抑郁或焦虑疾病，通常逐步起效；双相或精神病性症状可能需要其他药物方案。没有一种可以自行服用、立即保证安全的“去轻生药”。
text.en: SSRIs and other antidepressants treat appropriate depressive or anxiety disorders and usually work gradually. Bipolar or psychotic symptoms may need other regimens. There is no self-administered pill that immediately guarantees safety from suicidal action.

text.zh-CN: 开始抗抑郁药或调整剂量后，要留意烦躁、失眠和自杀想法的新出现或加重，25岁以下尤其需要关注；任何年龄都应及时报告。常见不适还包括恶心、头痛或性功能变化，医生可据此调整方案。
text.en: After starting or changing an antidepressant, watch for new or worsening agitation, sleep problems or suicidal thoughts, particularly under age25, and report changes promptly at any age. Nausea, headache and sexual effects can also guide treatment adjustments.

text.zh-CN: 把处方药、非处方药、草药和饮酒情况一并告诉医生或药师。按共同商定的方式保管和领取药物，避免大量无管理地存放；不要自行突然停药，有安全担忧时立即联系团队。
text.en: Tell the clinician or pharmacist about prescriptions, over-the-counter products, herbs and alcohol. Agree safe storage and dispensing instead of unmanaged stockpiles. Do not stop medicines abruptly; contact the team immediately about safety concerns.

text.zh-CN: 伴有抑郁、食欲差时，可以从规律进餐和容易准备的普通食物开始，请可信的人帮助采购或一起吃饭。这是维持身体需要和日常节律的办法，不能据此声称某种食物能治疗自杀意念。
text.en: With depression and poor appetite, regular meals and manageable ordinary food can support daily routine, with practical help obtaining or sharing meals. This maintains basic needs; it does not establish any food as treatment for suicidal thoughts.

text.zh-CN: 危机时避免用酒精或毒品压住感受，它们可能降低自控并加重冲动。草药或营养补充剂也可能与精神科药物相互作用，使用前告诉医生；有酒精或其他物质依赖者应由医疗团队安排治疗。
text.en: Avoid using alcohol or illicit drugs to suppress distress, because they may reduce restraint and worsen impulses. Herbs and supplements can interact with psychiatric medicines; discuss them first. Dependence requires a treatment plan with clinicians.

text.zh-CN: 可以直接而平静地问对方是否有自杀想法，听完再一起联系帮助，不争辩、羞辱或责怪。若对方表示可能行动，不承诺替其永久保密，要联系能协助保障安全的人或急救服务。
text.en: Ask calmly and directly about suicidal thoughts, listen and connect to help without argument, shame or blame. When the person may act, do not promise permanent secrecy; involve people or emergency services who can help maintain safety.

text.en: Keep the safety plan and contacts accessible, connect with agreed people and break today's tasks into manageable steps, prioritising company, sleep and treatment. Supporters also need shared help and rest rather than carrying all crisis care alone.

text.zh-CN: 儿童青少年的烦躁、拒学、被欺凌、关系冲突或突然退缩，可能需要儿童心理或精神科评估。不要因成年人看来事情“小”就否定痛苦；在适当保护隐私与安全的前提下联合家庭、学校及专业人员。
text.en: Irritability, school avoidance, bullying, relationship conflict or sudden withdrawal in children may need child mental-health assessment. An event seeming minor to an adult does not make distress trivial; coordinate family, school and clinicians with appropriate privacy and safety.

text.zh-CN: 孕期或产后出现自杀意念，要尽快联系产科和精神卫生团队；产后伴幻觉、混乱或明显行为异常需紧急评估。照护者应协助安排母婴安全和照料，不把这些表现当作普通疲劳或短暂情绪波动。
text.en: Suicidal thoughts during pregnancy or after childbirth need prompt maternity and mental-health contact. Postpartum hallucinations, confusion or major behavioural changes require urgent assessment. Arrange safety and practical care for parent and baby rather than assuming ordinary tiredness or transient mood changes.

text.en: Older adults may emphasise pain, emotional emptiness or memory problems. Discrimination, violence or poor support can also obstruct help-seeking. Assessment needs understandable communication and attention to care and living difficulties rather than treating an identity as a cause of illness.

text.zh-CN: 想法的强度可随压力、睡眠、用药和相关疾病变化。一次好转不表示所有困难已解决，反复出现也不代表治疗无望；随访要问实际功能、支持是否可用，以及安全计划是否需要改动。
text.en: Intensity can change with stress, sleep, medicines and associated illness. Initial improvement does not resolve every difficulty, and recurrence does not mean treatment is hopeless. Follow-up reviews daily function, available support and whether the safety plan needs revision.

text.zh-CN: 离开急诊或住院前确认接下来由谁联系、何时复诊及失联时怎么办。英国NICE建议：自伤后仍有安全担忧者，在心理社会评估后48小时内获得首次后续照护；这不是让当下有危险的人等待48小时。
text.en: Before leaving emergency or inpatient care, confirm who will make contact, the next appointment and what to do if contact fails. UK NICE recommends initial aftercare within48hours of psychosocial assessment after self-harm when safety concerns persist; immediate danger must not wait for that interval.

text.zh-CN: 复诊间隔内若出现行动意图、控制不住的冲动或安全支持中断，要立即使用危机计划并寻求紧急帮助；不要等到下次量表评分或常规复诊。
text.en: If intent, uncontrollable impulses or loss of safety support develops between visits, use the crisis plan and seek urgent help immediately rather than waiting for another score or routine appointment.

text.zh-CN: 持续被想法困住会影响工作学习、人际联系与自我照护，也会让帮助者疲惫。及早联系专业支持，是为了减少这些负担，而不是要求当事人靠意志独自克服。
text.en: Persistent preoccupation can disrupt work, study, relationships and self-care, and exhaust supporters. Early professional support reduces these burdens rather than expecting willpower alone to resolve them.

text.zh-CN: 最严重的结果是发生自伤、自杀未遂或死亡；未遂也可能造成长期身体损伤。已经受伤时，即便后来表示后悔或情绪平静，也仍需要及时医学评估和后续心理照护。
text.en: The most serious outcomes are self-injury, suicide attempts or death; an attempt can cause lasting physical injury. Injury requires prompt medical assessment and subsequent psychological care even if the person later regrets it or appears calm.

text.en: During a steadier period, agree a safety plan, reliable contacts and safe management of dangerous items. Help maintain treatment for pain, sleep, mental illness or substance problems, and activate contact when personal warning signs appear.

text.zh-CN: 家庭、学校和社区可以通过反欺凌、减少污名、提高求助可及性及负责任传播信息来降低障碍。没有措施能保证零风险，因此不应把后来发生的危机简单归咎于当事人或亲友。
text.en: Families, schools and communities can reduce barriers through anti-bullying support, less stigma, accessible help and responsible communication. Prevention cannot guarantee zero risk, so a later crisis should not be reduced to blame of the person or those close to them.
